saints.name: St. Paul VI
saints.title: Pope
saints.shortBlurb: The pope who carried the Second Vatican Council to its close and steered the Church through its reforms…
biography: Giovanni Battista Montini was born at Concesio, near Brescia, in 1897. Ordained in 1920, he served more than thirty years in the Secretariat of State and was among the closest advisers of Pope Pius XII, who named him Archbishop of Milan in 1954. Created a cardinal in 1958, he was elected pope in 1963 and took the name Paul VI.

He reconvened the Second Vatican Council and brought it to its close on 8 December 1965, then gave his pontificate to carrying out its reforms. The first pope of modern times to journey abroad, he embraced the Patriarch Athenagoras in the Holy Land in 1964, addressed the United Nations in New York in 1965, and travelled widely in Asia, Africa, and the Americas.

His 1968 encyclical Humanae Vitae, reaffirming the Church's teaching on married love, cost him much sympathy, yet he bore opposition with patience. He died at Castel Gandolfo on 6 August 1978 and was canonized by Pope Francis on 14 October 2018.
saints.knownFor: Guiding the Church through the close of the Second Vatican Council.
